title: Employees
text: Everyone who works here, where they work and their employment history.

list.empty_text: Hire the first person to start keeping records here.
list.none_text: Try another name or code, or clear the filters.

hire_page.title: Hire someone
hire_page.text: Their employee code is given when you save.
hire_page.no_probation: No probation here: they are confirmed at once.

fields.no_departments: This branch has no departments yet (HRM → Departments).

profile.not_found: This employee was not found, or is not part of this organization.
profile.conflict: Someone changed this employee a moment ago. The latest details are shown now; make your change again.
profile.revealed_note: Looking at the full ids is recorded in the audit log.

steps.exits_on_hint: Left empty: {count} days of notice from the effective date.
steps.exit_confirm_text: They will be marked as left from the last working day. Their records stay, and they can be rehired later.

documents.file_hint: PDF, JPG, PNG or WebP, up to {kb} KB.
documents.remove_text: The file is deleted. This is recorded in the audit log.
documents.empty_text: Contracts, certificates and copies of ids kept for this employee appear here.

positions.title: Designations
positions.text: Job titles people can hold here, in both languages.
positions.empty_text: Add the job titles of this organization, for example Teacher or Accountant.

no_access: You can see employees but not change them. Ask an owner for HR rights.

fields_page.title: Extra fields
fields_page.text: Details you ask about every employee here, beyond the usual ones (blood group, licence number, shift).
fields_page.at_limit: Switch one off to add another.
fields_page.empty_text: Add the details your organization keeps about people, for example blood group or a licence number.
fields_page.label: Name of the field
fields_page.key_hint: Used in import files; cannot change later.

import_page.title: Import employees
import_page.text: Add many people at once from a spreadsheet. Every row is checked first; nothing is saved until you start.
import_page.how_template: Download the template and open it in Excel or Google Sheets.
import_page.how_fill: Fill in one person per row. Always needed: {columns}.
import_page.how_save: Save as "CSV UTF-8" and choose the file below.
import_page.hint_kinds: permanent, contract, part_time, intern, daily_wage, or their names (Permanent, স্থায়ী)
import_page.hint_codes: codes shown in the app; the manager must already be an employee
import_page.unit_hint: A row can name another unit in unit_code.
import_page.file_hint: Up to {rows} people and {kb} KB per file.
import_page.running_note: You can leave this page; the import continues.
import_page.skip_one: Leave out the row with problems
import_page.skip_other: Leave out the {count} rows with problems
import_page.cancel_text: Nobody from this file is added. You can check a corrected file any time.
import_page.hint_department: the department's name (English or Bangla), within the row's branch
import_page.hint_role: a role name for the login (empty: the company's default roles)
import_page.create_logins: Also give each person a login with the company's first password
import_page.create_logins_hint: They sign in with the phone or email in the file and must choose their own password first.
import_page.logins_done: Logins: {created} new, {linked} already had an account, {failed} not given.

org_chart.title: Org chart
org_chart.text: Who reports to whom. Open a person to see the people who report to them.
org_chart.empty_text: Hire people and set their managers to see the org chart.
org_chart.toggle_one: Show or hide the person who reports to {name}
org_chart.toggle_other: Show or hide the {shown} people who report to {name}
org_chart.more_one: 1 more is not shown here. Use the employee list to find them.
org_chart.more_other: {shown} more are not shown here. Use the employee list to find them.

login.label: Login
login.none: Not linked: they cannot check in or see their own records yet.
login.title: Link a login
login.text: Choose the login {name} uses. They can then check in and see their own records.
login.empty: No other login of the company to link.
login.invite_text: They get an email to set their password, no sign-up, and are linked to this employee straight away.
login.or_existing: Or link a login they have already:
login.invited: Invitation sent to {email}; they are linked to this employee.
login.resent: A new link went to {email}; the old one no longer works.
login.unlink_text: {name} can no longer check in with it. Their records stay.

departments.title: Departments
departments.text: The departments of each branch and how many people work in each. A department head can be given rights over their department alone.
departments.all_hint: Write the name: the department is added to every branch that does not have it yet.
departments.all_text_one: It will be added to {count} branch.
departments.all_text_other: It will be added to {count} branches.
departments.close_blocked: People still work here: move them first
departments.close_text: Nobody can be hired into it or moved to it any more. Its records stay, and you can open it again later.
departments.reopen_text: People can be hired into it and moved to it again.
departments.empty_text: Add the departments of each branch, such as Accounts or Administration. Then choose one when hiring or moving someone.

first_login.page_text: The first password employees get, and the roles their logins start with. They choose their own password at first sign-in.
first_login.password_is_set: Set on {when} by {by}. It is kept hidden; type a new one to replace it.
first_login.password_not_set: Not set yet. Choose one before giving employees logins.
first_login.new_password: New first password (leave empty to keep it)
first_login.password_rules: At least 10 characters, with letters and numbers.
first_login.password_needed: Type the first password employees will get.
first_login.mismatch: The two passwords are not the same.
first_login.roles_text: What employees can see and do once they are in. A role chosen for one person or in the import's "role" column is used instead.
first_login.no_roles: There are no roles here yet. Make one in Settings → Roles.
first_login.how_1: Give a login from the employee list (many at once), an employee's page, or an import.
first_login.how_2: The employee signs in with their phone number or email and this password. It works for {days} days.
first_login.how_3: At first sign-in they must choose their own password. Until then nothing else opens.
first_login.how_4: Someone who already has an account keeps their own password; they only get access here.
first_login.title: Login with the first password
first_login.text: Signs in with {contact} and the company's first password (works for {days} days), then chooses their own.
first_login.not_set: The company has no first password yet.
first_login.given: {name} can sign in now with the first password.
first_login.linked: {name} already had an account: they got access with their own password.
first_login.reset_text: {name} signs in with the company's first password again and chooses their own. Any device they are signed in on is signed out.
first_login.many_text: Each signs in with their phone or email and the company's first password, then chooses their own.
first_login.many_done: {created} new logins, {linked} people who had an account, {failed} not given.
first_login.many_done_hint: Tell each person their first password in person, never by group message.
